\chapter{Hand and Money Join the Map}
\label{ch:gu-hand-money-map}
\hlchaptermodality{25}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can hear, say, read, and write five concrete Gujarati words, including hand and money.}

Hand and money enter meaning-first; one isolated ai-sign lesson unlocks \gu{પૈસા} before the five-word checkpoint scores all four skills separately.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[hāth]{\gu{હાથ} — hear hand first}

\label{lesson:GU-C21-hear-haath}



\begin{quote}
Say home. Now listen twice: \textbf{hāth} means \textbf{hand}. Keep its long vowel and final puff distinct from \emph{ghar}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Touch your hand when you hear \emph{hāth}, then say \emph{hāth} once from the meaning.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://gu.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%AA\%B5\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AB\%8B\%E0\%AA\%B6:\%E0\%AA\%B6\%E0\%AA\%AC\%E0\%AB\%8D\%E0\%AA\%A6\_\%E0\%AA\%85\%E0\%AA\%A8\%E0\%AB\%81\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AB\%8D\%E0\%AA\%B0\%E0\%AA\%AE\%E0\%AA\%A3\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AA\%BE}{Gujarati Wiktionary word index}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[hāth]{\gu{હાથ} — hand on the page}

\label{lesson:GU-C21-haath}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\gu{ઘર}}, then look:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\gu{હાથ}} — \emph{hāth} — hand
\end{quote}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\gu{હાથ}} once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://gu.wiktionary.org/wiki/\%E0\%AA\%B5\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AB\%8B\%E0\%AA\%B6:\%E0\%AA\%B6\%E0\%AA\%AC\%E0\%AB\%8D\%E0\%AA\%A6\_\%E0\%AA\%85\%E0\%AA\%A8\%E0\%AB\%81\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AB\%8D\%E0\%AA\%B0\%E0\%AA\%AE\%E0\%AA\%A3\%E0\%AA\%BF\%E0\%AA\%95\%E0\%AA\%BE}{Gujarati Wiktionary word index}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paisā]{\gu{પૈસા} — hear money first}

\label{lesson:GU-C21-hear-paisa}



\begin{quote}
Say hand. Now listen twice: \textbf{paisā} means \textbf{money}. Do not read the Gujarati shape yet; one vowel sign still needs its own tiny lesson.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Choose money or hand as you hear \emph{paisā} and \emph{hāth}. Then say \emph{paisā} from the meaning cue.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english-gujarati/money}{Cambridge English–Gujarati Dictionary: money}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ai vowel sign]{\gu{ૈ} — one sign for ai}

\label{lesson:GU-W21-ai-matra}



\begin{quote}
The attached sign \textbf{\gu{ૈ}} carries the \emph{ai} sound. It sits above a consonant; by itself here it is only a writing shape, not a word.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Watch the model: make the lower high arc from left to right, lift, then add the second higher arc from left to right. Trace \textbf{\gu{ૈ}} twice and copy it once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stroke-order source: \href{https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/}{t30apps Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice}, fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati form documented in \texttt{data/scripts/gujarati.json}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paisā]{\gu{પૈસા} — money on the page}

\label{lesson:GU-C21-paisa}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\gu{ૈ}}, then read \textbf{\gu{હાથ}}. Now look:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\gu{પૈસા}} — \emph{paisā} — money
\end{quote}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\gu{પૈસા}}, cover it, wait five seconds, and write it once more.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english-gujarati/money}{Cambridge English–Gujarati Dictionary: money}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bajār — ghar — mandir — hāth — paisā]{Retrieve five concrete words}

\label{lesson:GU-R21-travel-five}

Recall the three-place checkpoint, then say hand and money.

Hear all five in mixed order, say each from its meaning, read the five printed cards, then write the two words named aloud.

\section[bajār — ghar — mandir — hāth — paisā]{Payoff — five words in four skills}

\label{lesson:GU-C21-travel-five}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-place score, then say hand and money.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. Identify five heard words. 2. Produce five words from meaning cues. 3. Match five printed cards to meanings. 4. Write three heard words without a model.

Pass each skill separately. A strong score in one skill cannot replace a miss in another.
